page: Amazon Web Services c7g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors based on the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 core design. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at 2.6 GHz, featuring a single thread per core to eliminate noisy-neighbor issues common to simultaneous multithreading. Cache architecture comprises 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity sits at 32.0 GB, maintaining a compute-centric 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, while offering an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results place the c7g.4xlarge consistently in the middle tier for raw computational throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 12798.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 24503.13. Memory subsystem performance is a notable highlight: large-block uncached write bandwidth reached 93.97 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems alongside a strong PassMark memory score of 2972.27. Read performance remains solid with 186.18 GB/sec in large-block passes and 1551.75 GB/sec in cached small-block reads. Conversely, cryptographic throughput registered weaker results in PassMark encryption tests (2226.35), and prompt evaluation on 7B parameter language models reached only 28.19 tokens/sec, reflecting the architectural limitations of pure CPU inference on larger transformer architectures.

Qualitatively, the c7g.4xlarge provides strong resource density and cost efficiency by coupling custom ARM silicon with dedicated physical cores. Because each vCPU corresponds directly to a physical execution core without hyperthreading, CPU-bound workloads avoid resource contention. The lack of built-in local SSDs necessitates external network storage for persistent or high-I/O requirements, but the 8 Gbps network pipe ensures sufficient baseline connectivity. The instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads that align well with arm64 architectures, such as software compilation pipelines (evidenced by a Clang score of 20737.0), distributed caching with Redis (26.15 million SET ops/sec), multi-threaded data compression, microservices, and static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by 16 physical cores of AWS Graviton3 (ARM Neoverse-V1) silicon at 2.6 GHz running on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with a dedicated 1-to-1 core-to-thread topology, it pairs 16 vCPUs with 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps. It includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs. In empirical tests, the instance demonstrates strong memory write throughput of 93.97 GB/sec and solid general compute performance, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 12798.0 and a Clang compilation score of 20737.0. While cryptographic benchmarking and mid-sized LLM prompt processing exhibit lower efficiency, its dedicated ARM cores offer high cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads such as Clang builds, high-throughput Redis caching, web serving, and containerized microservices.
